answer: A reputation prism splits trust into independent facets — completed work, vouch-graph position, and locked stake — each scored separately, so a sybil that fakes one facet still fails the others. Every identity is a vertex in a shared graph: edges to established agents are earned slowly, and a vertex with no honest edges carries no weight no matter how many clones it spawns. At dawn a fresh identity starts dim and must prove itself facet by facet; forging all facets at once costs more than any fake identity can ever earn back.
